title: The main reason is
details:
Example: The main reason is the cost.

Usage: Neutral; introduce the most important cause.

title: What it comes down to is
description: This is the essential deciding factor.
details:
Example: What it comes down to is trust.

Usage: Conversational; reduce a complex issue to its core.

title: Given the circumstances
details:
Example: Given the circumstances, we did well.

Usage: Neutral; judge something in its context.

title: For the sake of
description: For the benefit or purpose of.
details:
Example: For the sake of clarity, I’ll repeat that.

Usage: Neutral; state a purpose or beneficiary.

title: In light of
details:
Example: In light of the forecast, we’ll stay home.

Usage: Formal; explain a decision based on evidence.

title: That’s why
details:
Example: The road was closed; that’s why I’m late.

Usage: Neutral; link a cause to its consequence.

title: As a result
details:
Example: The boiler broke; as a result, we had no hot water.

Usage: Neutral; introduce an effect.

title: To some extent
details:
Example: To some extent, I agree.

Usage: Neutral; qualify how far a claim applies.

title: In other words
details:
Example: It’s optional; in other words, you can say no.

Usage: Neutral; clarify by rephrasing.

title: For instance
details:
Example: Try a local class, for instance, pottery.

Usage: Neutral; illustrate a broader point.

title: The way I see it
details:
Example: The way I see it, we have two options.

Usage: Conversational; frame your interpretation.

title: On the grounds that
details:
Example: They refused on the grounds that it was unsafe.

Usage: Formal; give a justification, often for a decision.

title: That said
details:
Example: It’s expensive. That said, it lasts for years.

Usage: Neutral; introduce a balancing point.

title: Even so
details:
Example: It was raining; even so, we went out.

Usage: Neutral; a result contrary to expectations.

title: Unless I’m mistaken
details:
Example: Unless I’m mistaken, we’ve met before.

Usage: Neutral; soften a factual assertion.

title: It stands to reason
details:
Example: It stands to reason that more staff would help.

Usage: Neutral; indicate an apparently obvious inference.

title: There’s more to it than that
details:
Example: Price matters, but there’s more to it than that.

Usage: Conversational; challenge an oversimplification.

title: That doesn’t necessarily mean
details:
Example: It’s expensive, but that doesn’t necessarily mean it’s better.

Usage: Neutral; separate evidence from an assumption.

title: Taking everything into account
details:
Example: Taking everything into account, we should wait.

Usage: Neutral; introduce an overall judgement.

title: On balance
details:
Example: On balance, the move was worth it.

Usage: Neutral; state a considered conclusion.
